task_title: Add spell-skill rows to combat skills HUD

plan_review.notes: Alt A (expandable/pageable tracker) and Alt B (per-slot skill indicators on HudAbilityBar) were both weighed against the chosen fixed-2-row extension of HudSkillTracker; both add material input/layout complexity for a combat HUD where 3+ simultaneously-equipped trackable spells is an edge case, not the common case, so neither displaced the chosen design (divergence=minor, not major_fork). Concerns resolved: (1) BLOCKING - silent 2-row cap could hide skills when >2 trackable spells equipped -> added a non-blocking +N overflow indicator in the title strip (countMatchingSpellSkills) plus a unit test, so the cap is now visible instead of silent; (2) unarmed/spell-only visibility gap -> confirmed non-applicable: getActiveWeaponDef(world) is never undefined during real gameplay (equipmentSystem.ts always calls setActiveWeaponDef on spawn/equip), so panel-hidden-when-unarmed is not a reachable player state; (3) panel mislabeled WEAPON SKILLS after adding spell rows -> renamed title to SKILLS; (4) shared-threshold-drift foot-gun -> confirmed the game-layer registry already generates all 10 spell skills from one array literal (SPELL_SKILL_THRESHOLDS spread via .map), so there is structurally one source of truth, not two; added a regression test asserting every spell skill still uses SPELL_SKILL_THRESHOLDS so a future divergent-curve edit cannot silently break the HUD; (5) automated coverage weaker than runtime behavior -> accepted as consistent with the existing HudSkillTracker/HudAbilityBar test convention in this repo (pure-logic unit tests + source-regex wiring test + e2e visual-regression test, no Phaser-scene HUD test harness exists for any HUD widget); mitigated further by a real hud-lab manual verification with seeded world.skillStatesByEntity confirming the reused progress-bar math renders correctly for a spell skill (fill grew 2.5px -> 82px on usage change).

independent_grade.notes: The implementation correctly expands the HUD skill tracker with pure, easily testable logic for spell rows and overflow handling. Scope is tightly bounded and appropriately leverages the shared layer to safely share thresholds across engine and game layers without violating import rules. Testing covers pure functions, wiring invariants, and data-layer threshold constraints. No bugs or policy violations found.
